title: India’s Semiconductor Ecosystem Needs Taiwan’s SMEs to Build a Deep Tech Corridor
gist: India's semiconductor push consists of discrete deals (Tata-ASML, PSMC, Renesas, KABIL) rather than an ecosystem, and the piece argues India should stop chasing a TSMC-style anchor tenant — which is heading to the U.S. instead — and instead build an India-Taiwan Deep Tech Corridor modeled on Hsinchu Science Park's SME density, using India's US$19,245 engineer salaries (six times below the U.S.) and cultural infrastructure to attract mid-sized Taiwanese firms.

insights.claim: India's electronics value-chain push currently rests on discrete interventions — KABIL critical mineral procurement, a Tata Electronics-ASML MoU for lithography tools at the Dholera fab, PSMC technology transfer for mature-node production, and Renesas advanced-node design investment.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Maps the specific counterparties already committed to Indian semis — but the deal-by-deal structure means no compounding supplier base yet.
insights.locator: India’s ambition to become a key player

insights.claim: India's electronics exports stood at US$48 billion as of 2026 with smartphones alone at US$31 billion, evidencing that the sector sits at the downstream assembly end of the value chain rather than in core manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Two-thirds of India's electronics export headline is phone assembly — a thin-margin base that overstates India's real position in the chip supply chain.

insights.claim: Financial and policy incentives from India's central and state governments have helped but fall short of the global opportunity, and a strategy of raising value-add through incentives alone is unlikely to be effective.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Bearish read on India's subsidy-led semiconductor strategy — subsidies cannot buy the supplier density that determines where fabs actually locate.

insights.claim: Malaysia and Vietnam are the preferred near-shoring destinations for major electronics manufacturers, and Taiwan's exports as of May 2026 concentrate in China, the United States, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, and Vietnam — supply chains that cannot be replicated in India quickly.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: India is not currently in Taiwan's export orbit at all — a structural gap that makes India a multi-year, not near-term, electronics substitution story.

themes.theme: Anchor-tenant strategy is the wrong bet

insights.claim: Large Taiwanese firms like TSMC are leaning toward U.S. rather than Indian investment because of market demand, U.S. tariffs, and the geopolitical drive to diversify electronics beyond China, so India cannot count on an anchor-tenant spillover effect.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Discount Indian narratives that a marquee foundry announcement is imminent; capital allocation from Taiwan's majors is politically routed to the U.S.

insights.claim: Taiwan's expansion into the United States will be expensive because the U.S. lacks industrial clusters comparable to Taiwan's science parks and because the two countries' labor cultures differ.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Explains the persistent cost overruns at U.S. fab projects: cluster absence and labor-culture mismatch are structural, not transitional, cost drivers.
insights.locator: Taiwan’s expansion into the United States will be expensive

insights.claim: Splitting Taiwanese investment between the United States and India, anchored by long-term supply agreements with U.S. companies, would reduce concentration risk while solving labor shortages in both the U.S. and Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete policy template to watch: U.S.-offtake-backed Taiwanese investment in India would be the signal that the corridor thesis is becoming real.

insights.claim: The average annual semiconductor engineer salary in 2026 is US$122,650 in the United States versus US$57,436 in Taiwan and about US$19,245 in India — roughly three times below Taiwan and six times below the U.S.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Quantifies the labor arbitrage that could pull back-end and design work to India — and the wage gap U.S. fabs must absorb permanently.

insights.claim: Because semiconductor fabrication runs around the clock, TSMC's Arizona facilities must either staff three eight-hour shifts or deploy manufacturing automation not yet demonstrated at scale in advanced semiconductor assembly.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: The three-shift labor multiplier is the underappreciated reason U.S. fab operating costs stay structurally above Taiwan's regardless of subsidies.
insights.locator: Since semiconductor fabrication runs around the clock

insights.claim: Taiwan cannot backfill even a small offshore shift of its semiconductor production from its own workforce, as analysts flag demand-supply imbalances in its skilled factory labor compounded by declining birth rates.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Taiwan's demographic ceiling is a hard constraint on global fab expansion — a durable bid for automation vendors and for offshore engineering hubs.
insights.locator: Even if a small portion of Taiwan’s semiconductor production

insights.claim: India is a net exporter of engineering talent and offers geographic proximity to the Asian manufacturing belt spanning Malaysia, Vietnam, and the Philippines.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: India's comparative advantage is engineering headcount plus logistics adjacency, not fabrication capability — favoring design and ATP roles.
insights.locator: India is also considered a net exporter of engineering talent

themes.theme: Deep Tech Corridor as ecosystem density

insights.claim: A Deep Tech Corridor is proposed as an amalgamation of transnational industrial clusters with cosmopolitan social and cultural settings, providing an interconnected web of component suppliers, specialist service firms, technical talent, start-ups, and institutional knowledge.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Reframes semiconductor localization as a cluster-density problem rather than a capex problem — a useful test for judging any national chip strategy.
insights.quote: an amalgamation of transnational industrial clusters with cosmopolitan social and cultural settings that would encourage cross-border innovation
insights.locator: To address this, India should develop a Deep Tech Corridor

insights.claim: Hsinchu Science Park is the precedent for the proposed corridor because its competitiveness derives not from one large anchor company but from a dense network of SMEs, research institutions, and support services.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: The SME-density model implies the investable opportunity in India semis is mid-cap component and services suppliers, not a single mega-fab.
insights.quote: Its competitiveness is derived not from one large anchor company but from a dense network of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), research institutions, and support services.
insights.locator: Importantly, the proposed Deep Tech Corridor has a clear precedent

insights.claim: Reducing perceived cultural distance through international schools, multilingual administrative and legal services, and sister-city residential districts partnered with Hsinchu, Taichung, and Tainan is treated as core investment infrastructure, not soft policy.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Identifies a non-obvious binding constraint on FDI: expatriate livability determines whether long-term Taiwanese commitments materialize.
insights.locator: Social and cultural infrastructure includes international schools

insights.claim: Concrete corridor building blocks already exist, including a T-Works Telangana talent-exchange agreement with Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute and a Mizoram government agreement to send 50 youths to Taiwan for high-tech training.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: State-level India-Taiwan links are running ahead of national policy — Telangana is the leading indicator state for this corridor.
insights.locator: One example is a collaboration between T-Works in Telangana

insights.claim: The emerging technology frontiers of AI hardware, nanomaterials, solid-state batteries, and quantum computing all depend on semiconductor supply chains that are simultaneously geographically diversified and technically deep.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Frames chip-supply-chain geography as the upstream bottleneck for four separate frontier-tech investment themes at once.

insights.claim: India's eventual role in global electronics — research partner, component manufacturer, or fabrication node — will be determined by the industrial infrastructure and integrated technology ecosystem it builds now, with Taiwan treated as a structural co-builder rather than a guest.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Sets the near-term decision window as decisive — a policy failure now locks India into low-value assembly for the next technology cycle.
insights.quote: not as guests but as structural co-builders of a shared industrial base
